paragraphs: Heimdall Power sells sensors and software to electric utilities, with capacity tools meant to help them safely adjust transmission limits, improve operational planning and stay compliant with industry standards. The company was founded in Norway in 2016.

Its dynamic line rating offering combines physical and virtual Neurons to take real-time, on-line measurements. The sensors report temperature, current and inclination on the conductor. Deployment is handled by an autonomous drone installation system that the company says places Neurons in remote or hard-to-reach areas. A facility ratings module consolidates all ratings into one unified system and is aimed at simplifying NERC FAC-008 compliance. Further tools give grid operators real-time visibility into threats like icing, line movement, electrical faults and wildfire risks.

The about page states that the company has grown 10x in two years, raised a $25M Series B and expanded with a North American headquarters in Charlotte, NC. A news item on the site reports that Heimdall Power was selected by Statnett for a new Dynamic Line Rating project.

quote.text: Autonomous Drone Installation System ensures fast, safe deployment of Neurons in remote or hard-to-reach areas.
